thread:
maya: Hey SDK team — hitting a weird parity issue in the onboarding sample app. Admin listModels via curl returns 200+payload but via Node SDK it returns 422. Repro steps below, super small thread so pinging here first.

maya: curl that works:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Id: sample-app" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/models
```

maya: Node snippet that fails (sdk v2.3.1):
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.TOKEN })
await client.admin.listModels({})
```

maya: Logs show the server getting the request but x-client-id is missing; SDK log shows `x-request-source: sdk` is present. Also noticed the SDK retries immediately once and then succeeds with a duplicate create in one flow — not sure if related. :facepalm:

ben: Thanks for the repro. Can you paste the full network trace (headers) and the exact SDK package hash? Also can you confirm Node version?

maya: node 18.16, sdk 2.3.1 (sha: 9f2b7). Network trace snippet: server received Authorization and x-request-source but NO x-client-id. SDK did not send the custom header I passed in older sample-apps. I tried passing headers in options but sdk strips unknown headers by default.

ben: Ah — that's the key. We introduced header normalization in 2.x to prevent header leaks, but the whitelist accidentally omitted `X-Client-Id`. That explains the missing header. The retry behavior you saw is also plausible: the 2.x default retry changed to a linear immediate retry on 5xx with jitter=0 to prioritize latency; that can cause duplicate side-effecting operations if server does a 5xx after processing.

olivia: Does this impact the onboarding funnel materially? If sample-apps can't list models, new teams will get a broken first impression.

maya: Yeah onboarding is blocked for me until I workaround. Workaround: fork the SDK and set allowCustomHeaders=true or patch the whitelist locally. But that's not viable for general customers.

ben: Plan: I'll open a patch to add `X-Client-Id` to the header whitelist and revert the retry policy default to exponential backoff for idempotency-sensitive admin endpoints. Quick PR queued: https://github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/1234. Can do a 2.3.2 canary release to devex org.

ben: Short-term mitigation: you can pass `{ headers: { 'X-Client-Id': 'sample-app' }, allowCustomHeaders: true }` when constructing client. We'll document this in the sample-app readme until patch lands.

olivia: Please also add a changelog entry and migration note — call out the behavioral change to retries and header normalization so customers know. We should add an integration test in CI that runs the sample-app against a mock admin endpoint to catch regressions.

maya: I can validate the canary once it's out and post the request-id: req_abc123 so you can trace. Incidentally, the SDK log line where it normalizes headers looks like: `normalizeHeaders(headers) -> sanitizedHeaders` — we should log original vs sanitized when debug enabled so DE can triage quicker.

ben: Good call. I'll add a debug flag to emit header diffs under --sdk-debug. Rollout plan: canary to devex and devex-sample org for 24h, monitor errors, then patch to stable.

ci-bot: deploy queued: canary/sdk-2.3.2-rc.1 -> devex-canary (pipeline #4589).

maya: I'll test once it lands, thanks! :thumbsup:

ben: Thanks — opened followups: add whitelist test, add retry policy per-route config, migration note for 2.x.

olivia: Assign a quick task to DE to update the onboarding doc and sample-app to set `allowCustomHeaders` where appropriate so new users aren't blocked while we patch.

maya: Will do and post results here.
